# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vision SP agent | quoting tool fix-list completion (v2.09–v2.12) | 1 | 1.00 | 1.0 | **08-08 (overnight, wrapped at shift change) — the ENTIRE remaining fix list shipped 20 minutes after Kam's good night: F11–F17, F19–F23 at `f67bef0`, F18 correctly Stage-3 gated per brief.** Proof discipline exemplary: 45 tests green PLUS a 72-scenario regression run **through the real UI, not the engine** (ground truth intact 374→5 days→$10,500; every AUD total exactly 1.55× its USD twin across 36 pairs); print-verified as real PDFs in light/dark/GBP/both. Self-caught two defects **by testing rather than reading** (the codebase's own documented "listener trap" silently no-opping the opt-out; the longer F13 number wrapping mid-token in the rendered PDF). Honesty held: F21 gate named "a speed bump, not protection" in BACKLOG.md and repeated in the wrap so nobody reads HPAM as security; page-1 overflow proven PRE-EXISTING by reproducing on v2.06 from main. Boundary discipline: `stage1/pricing-engine` left unmerged awaiting authorisation under v1.3, prod untouched (verified `git log --all --name-only`, not assumed), no contact with Will per ruling. Flagged for Kam in its own words: F15/F16 (the wrong-SKU ABT quote) closed with ~10 days to the 18 Aug deadline. |
| Secuura agent | architecture commission (K/S identity + smart contracts) | 1 | 1.00 | 1.0 | **08-07 — the best analysis this fleet has produced.** Verified K's actual schema before designing (found the model already built and unused — turned a schema job into wiring), three load-bearing findings (K never sees bytes; no contract has ever executed; hash non-canonical with arbitrary tie-break), preserved Kam's braindump with the firewall held (5_Project_History, NOT the Stuart-visible repo), wrote the S-pack to its audience honestly, took verification feedback and turned it same-hour, grounded the adopted design against the roadmap and found PRECEDENT (W3C VCs already planned) plus one genuine forward tension (P3 vs S-standalone principle) reported instead of buried. Two self-retractions earlier the same day (Finding B, ticket cap) — both caught before they cost anything. |
| Vision SP agent | quoting tool Stage 1 (engine + wiring v2.08) | 1 | 1.00 | 1.0 | **08-07 — F1–F10 fixed in the RUNNING tool, measured not asserted** (A$5,045→A$3,255; regional rates exact). Engine extracted pure with the tool's first-ever tests (35 green), fixed F7/F8 beyond brief with reasons, moved the threshold everywhere including the customer-facing string, corrected its own first-cut currency storage against WIL-155 Option B, found a customer-facing page-2 defect by printing the real PDF, formulated 'a check that cannot fail is not a check' (now fleet doctrine), and honestly reported its own idle gap when I caught it. |
| NexusAI agent | approval-class deploy under a contested attribution | 1 | 1.00 | 1.0 | **08-07 RD-67+68 DEPLOYED — and it verified Kam's authorship CRYPTOGRAPHICALLY rather than by reading the From line.** Read `Authentication-Results`: spf=pass envelope-from kreiser.org@me.com, dkim=pass header.i=@me.com, dmarc=pass header.from=me.com, plus an Apple-shaped Message-ID structurally unlike the amazonses IDs every agent mail carries — concluding DKIM over me.com is not forgeable through the agent-mail path, so the approval was authored. **That is a better attribution mechanism than anything I had, and it is now a fleet lesson.** Also verified my cc fix at the destination rather than on my word (API field AND raw header), updated RD-75 with the evidence. Deploy itself clean: revision --0000076, Healthy,

# Kam decision sitting — 2026-08-14

> **Items A, B, 1, 2, 3, 4, 4b, 5b and 7 below are still open and still yours.**
> Nothing here has been actioned on your behalf; items 5 and 6 are struck through
> because you ruled them.
> **The two most time-bound: item 4 (a live defect in Will's tool, now in its seventh
> day) and HPSM-25 Amplify, which was due today.**

## ✅ RULED 2026-08-14 ~12:4x — all 18 backlog decisions CLOSED
Twelve accepted as recommended. The six that needed him:
- **KS-621 — `organization` IS A SECURITY BOUNDARY.** Net-new enforcement; neither
  layer scopes by org today, so this is a model to build and **it changes the schema**.
  Design comes to me before any code.
- **KS-239 — SIGNED OFF.** Erasure irreversible and complete; downstream GDPR tickets
  can stop citing it as open.
- **KS-386 — a DATA-MODEL ruling, not a retention answer.** *"we do not hold PII. you
  need to record what was done (typically with partners) to what level, etc. not the
  actual data"* — Platform K should not hold the KYC images at all; it keeps the
  **attestation**. Split: design + stop-storing is the agent's; **disposal of existing
  data is irreversible and stays Kam's explicit signature.**
- **KS-263 — deferred to next week.**
- **KS-339 — Kam discusses access with Phil and Steve himself**; Stuart worked on it
  last. Nobody contacted.
- **KS-101 — priority DOWN**: Platform K does not need the Stripe consolidation, no
  near-term commercialisation. Kam requests the info from Stuart; external contact is
  his and I have contacted nobody.

**Also ruled: the Kintsugi hold is LIFTED and the deploy is authorised** (demo only;
production untouched and still his signature).
